<skill_content name="c4-review">
# Skill: c4-review

# C4 Review

Review C4 architecture models for notation compliance, completeness, and common mistakes.

## When to Use

- Reviewing a PR that modifies `architecture/workspace.dsl`
- Auditing an existing C4 model for quality
- Before publishing or sharing architecture diagrams
- After significant model changes to catch regressions
- When onboarding to understand if an existing model is trustworthy

## Required Inputs

1. Path to the Structurizr DSL workspace file (typically `architecture/workspace.dsl`)
2. Optionally: the project's technology stack and deployment context for completeness checks

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Syntax Validation

Run structurizr/structurizr to catch syntax errors before manual review:

Run Structurizr with the most native OCI runtime available, written `$RUNTIME` below: `container` on Apple Silicon macOS (after `container system start`), `wslc` on Windows where available, otherwise `podman` (Docker works too). Pin a dated image tag rather than `latest`, which moves: a newer release can reject a model an older one accepted. On a Linux host with SELinux, add `:z` to the volume.

```bash
$RUNTIME run --rm \
  -v "$(pwd):/work" \
  structurizr/structurizr:2026.09.19 validate -w /work/architecture/workspace.dsl
```

Mount the project root (not just `architecture/`) so `!adrs` / `!docs` symlinks resolve.

If validation fails, fix syntax errors first. Do not proceed with review until the model parses cleanly.

### Phase 2: Workspace Inspection

Run the `inspect` subcommand to surface Checkstyle-style violations (missing descriptions, duplicate names, duplicate view keys, duplicate relationship descriptions, etc.):

```bash
$RUNTIME run --rm \
  -v "$(pwd):/work" \
  structurizr/structurizr:2026.09.19 inspect -w /work/architecture/workspace.dsl -s error,warning
```

The exit code equals the number of violations. Severity levels can be tuned per element via `structurizr.inspection.*` workspace properties (`ignore`, `info`, `warning`, `error`).

### Phase 3: Element Review (manual)

Check every element in the model against these criteria:

#### People/Actors
- [ ] Every person has a clear, specific name (not "User" unless truly generic)
- [ ] Every person has a description stating their role/goal
- [ ] No duplicate people representing the same role
- [ ] External vs internal actors are distinguished (via tags or naming)

#### Software Systems
- [ ] Your system has a name and description
- [ ] External systems are clearly identified (tagged "External" or similar)
- [ ] Each external system has a description explaining what it provides
- [ ] No system is modeled that should actually be a container (e.g., a database you own)
- [ ] System names are unique and unambiguous

#### Containers
- [ ] Every container represents a **runtime boundary** (separately running process or data store)
- [ ] No libraries, modules, or packages modeled as containers
- [ ] Every container has a technology specified
- [ ] Every container has a meaningful description (not just restating the name)
- [ ] Database containers use the "Database" tag for cylinder shape
- [ ] No containers that should be external systems (services you don't own/deploy)

#### Components (if present)
- [ ] Components represent architecturally significant groupings, not just folder structure
- [ ] Every component has technology specified
- [ ] Components are within a single container (not spanning containers)
- [ ] The component diagram adds genuine value (if not, recommend removing it)

### Phase 4: Relationship Review

Check every relationship:

#### Labels
- [ ] Every relationship has a label describing **intent** (what is communicated, not just "uses")
- [ ] Labels match the arrow direction (source does X **to** destination)
- [ ] No vague labels: flag "Uses", "Connects to", "Interacts with", "Communicates with"

Suggest specific alternatives for vague labels:
| Vague | Ask | Better Example |
|-------|-----|----------------|
| "Uses" | What does it use it for? | "queries order history from" |
| "Connects to" | What data flows? | "sends email notifications via" |
| "Interacts with" | What's the interaction? | "submits search queries to" |
| "Communicates with" | What's communicated? | "publishes order events to" |

#### Technology
- [ ] Inter-container relationships specify protocol/technology (e.g., "JSON/HTTPS", "SQL/TCP", "gRPC", "AMQP")
- [ ] Intra-container relationships (component-to-component) may omit technology
- [ ] Person-to-container relationships specify the interface technology (e.g., "HTTPS", "WebSocket")

#### Direction
- [ ] Arrows point in the direction of dependency or data flow
- [ ] No bidirectional relationships (split into two if needed)
- [ ] Implied relationships make sense (e.g., user → container implies user → system)

### Phase 5: View Review

Check each view:

#### System Context View
- [ ] Exists (required for all projects)
- [ ] Shows the system at center with all users and external systems
- [ ] Uses `include *` or explicitly includes all relevant elements
- [ ] Has a descriptive title
- [ ] Does NOT include internal containers or components
- [ ] Does NOT include technology details (keep it non-technical)

#### Container View
- [ ] Exists (required for all projects)
- [ ] Shows all containers within the system boundary
- [ ] Includes people and external systems that interact with containers
- [ ] Has a descriptive title
- [ ] Does NOT include deployment details (clustering, load balancing, replication)
- [ ] Does NOT show components (those belong in component views)

#### Component View (if present)
- [ ] Scoped to a single container
- [ ] Only created for containers where internal structure matters
- [ ] Not just mirroring the code's package structure

#### Dynamic View (if present)
- [ ] Clearly scoped to a specific feature or use case
- [ ] Interactions are numbered in sequence
- [ ] Includes only elements involved in the specific flow

#### Deployment View (if present)
- [ ] Scoped to a specific environment (production, staging, etc.)
- [ ] Shows deployment nodes, not just containers
- [ ] Infrastructure nodes (load balancers, DNS, firewalls) are included where relevant

### Phase 6: Style Review

- [ ] People use `shape Person`
- [ ] Databases use `shape Cylinder`
- [ ] Colors are consistent across diagram types
- [ ] External elements are visually distinct from internal ones
- [ ] Tags are used for styling (not hardcoded per element)
- [ ] Consider color blindness — don't rely on color alone to convey meaning

### Phase 7: Completeness Check

- [ ] All known users/personas are represented
- [ ] All external system integrations are modeled
- [ ] All major containers are present (web app, API, database, queues, etc.)
- [ ] Relationships cover all known communication paths
- [ ] No orphaned elements (elements with no relationships)
- [ ] System context and container views exist at minimum

### Phase 8: Structural Issues

- [ ] `!identifiers hierarchical` is used (recommended for non-trivial models)
- [ ] Identifiers are descriptive (`api`, `database`, not `c1`, `c2`)
- [ ] Tags are used consistently for element types
- [ ] Groups are used for logical organization where helpful
- [ ] `!adrs` directive points to ADR directory (if ADRs exist)
- [ ] `!docs` directive points to documentation (if applicable)

## Output Format

Produce a review summary with:

1. **Validation result**: Pass/fail from structurizr/structurizr `validate`
2. **Inspection violations**: Count and categorization from structurizr/structurizr `inspect`
3. **Issues found**: Categorized as:
   - **Error**: Incorrect abstraction, missing required elements, wrong notation
   - **Warning**: Vague labels, missing descriptions, potential confusion
   - **Suggestion**: Style improvements, optional views, organizational improvements
4. **Completeness assessment**: What's missing relative to the known system
5. **Positive observations**: What the model does well (helps calibrate quality)

## Common Anti-Patterns

### The "Everything Uses Everything" Model
- Too many relationships with vague labels
- Fix: remove implied relationships, make labels specific

### The "Code Structure Mirror"
- Components that exactly match package/module structure
- Fix: model architecturally significant groupings, not code organization

### The "Missing Middle"
- System context exists but no container view, jumping straight to components
- Fix: always create the container view

### The "Stale Component Diagram"
- Component diagram that hasn't been updated as code evolved
- Fix: delete it or regenerate it; stale diagrams are worse than none

### The "Docker Confusion"
- Modeling Docker containers as C4 containers, or modeling C4 containers as Docker containers
- Fix: C4 containers are runtime boundaries; Docker is a deployment mechanism (belongs in deployment view)

### The "Technology Soup"
- Container descriptions that are just technology names ("Elixir GenServer Phoenix")
- Fix: descriptions should state responsibilities ("Handles user authentication and session management")

### The "GenServer Container"
- Individual GenServers modeled as C4 containers
- Fix: GenServers are BEAM processes within a VM — they're code-level, not runtime boundaries. Model the release as the container.

### The "Supervision Tree Diagram"
- Component diagram that mirrors the supervision tree structure
- Fix: components should represent functional groupings (Accounts, Orders, Notifications), not supervision hierarchies (Application → Supervisor → Worker)

### The "Umbrella = Microservices" Model
- Each umbrella app modeled as a separate C4 container or even software system
- Fix: if the umbrella deploys as one release, it's one container. Model umbrella apps as components within that container. Only split into containers if they deploy as separate releases.

## Erlang/Elixir/OTP Review Checklist

When reviewing a C4 model for an Elixir/OTP system, check these additional items:

### Abstraction Correctness
- [ ] OTP releases are modeled as containers (not individual applications or GenServers)
- [ ] GenServers, Agents, Tasks are NOT modeled as containers or components (unless architecturally significant)
- [ ] Supervisor trees are NOT reflected in the component structure
- [ ] Umbrella apps deployed as a single release are modeled as ONE container with components, not multiple containers
- [ ] Phoenix PubSub is NOT modeled as a separate message queue container
- [ ] ETS tables are NOT modeled as separate database containers (they're in-process)

### Container Review
- [ ] Phoenix application container specifies "Elixir/Phoenix" as technology, not just "Elixir"
- [ ] If Oban is embedded in the Phoenix release, it's a component, not a separate container
- [ ] If Broadway is embedded, it's a component, not a separate container
- [ ] Mnesia is only a separate container if it's architecturally significant and spans nodes
- [ ] Nerves firmware is modeled as a container, not a software system

### Relationship Review
- [ ] Ecto connections specify "Ecto/TCP" or "SQL/TCP", not just "Ecto"
- [ ] WebSocket connections are labeled (for LiveView, Channels)
- [ ] Erlang distribution between nodes is modeled as a deployment-level relationship, not a container-level one
- [ ] Oban job queues via PostgreSQL are labeled "Oban/PostgreSQL", not just "PostgreSQL"

### Component Review (if present)
- [ ] Components represent functional domains (Accounts, Orders, Notifications), not OTP applications or supervision trees
- [ ] Phoenix contexts or Ash domains map naturally to components (they're the intended grouping mechanism)
- [ ] Ecto.Repo is either a component ("Data Access") or omitted — not a separate container
- [ ] Technology labels use Elixir ecosystem terms: "Phoenix", "Ecto", "Oban", "Broadway", "Swoosh", "LiveView", "Ash Domain", "AshJsonApi", "AshGraphql"

### Ash Framework Review (if applicable)
- [ ] Ash domains are modeled as components, not containers (they're logical boundaries within the release)
- [ ] Individual Ash resources are NOT modeled as components (they're code-level, like classes)
- [ ] No separate "Data Access" or "Repo" component — Ash handles persistence internally
- [ ] AshJsonApi / AshGraphql are reflected in the API component technology, not as separate containers
- [ ] Ash domain components don't duplicate the resource list — describe domain responsibility instead

### Deployment Review (if present)
- [ ] BEAM VM is modeled as a deployment node hosting the release
- [ ] Erlang distribution / clustering is shown between BEAM nodes
- [ ] EPMD or DNS-based discovery is an infrastructure node (if architecturally relevant)
- [ ] Hot code upgrades, if used, are noted in deployment node properties

## Validation

The review is complete when:

- `validate` passes (the model parses cleanly) and the `inspect` violation count has been triaged
- Every phase checklist (elements, relationships, views, style, completeness, structure) has been walked
- The Output Format summary is produced with issues categorized Error / Warning / Suggestion

## Related Skills

- `c4-model` — C4 abstractions and diagram types
- `structurizr-dsl` — DSL syntax reference
- `c4-deployment` — Deployment modeling specifics

Base directory for this skill: /work/.opencode/skills/c4-review
Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.

const dsl = `workspace "Fleet Manager" "Manages a regional car rental fleet." {
    model {
        customer = person "Customer" "Rents vehicles through the fleet manager."
        manager = softwareSystem "Fleet Manager" "Manages bookings, vehicles, contracts, and maintenance." {
            booking = container "Booking Web App" "Lets customers book and return vehicles." "Python"
            mobile = container "Mobile Backend" "Serves the rental mobile app." "Kotlin"
            fleet = container "Fleet Service" "Tracks vehicle availability and locations." "Java"
            dispatch = container "Dispatch Service" "Assigns vehicles to bookings." "Java"
            pricing = container "Pricing Service" "Calculates rental prices." "Go"
            maintenance = container "Maintenance Service" "Plans servicing and repairs." "C#"
            telemetry = container "Telemetry Ingest" "Collects vehicle telemetry events." "Go"
            notifications = container "Notification Service" "Sends booking and reminder messages." "Python"
            contracts = container "Contract Service" "Manages rental contracts and deposits." "Java"
            damage = container "Damage Assessment" "Records and prices vehicle damage." "Python"
            reports = container "Reports Service" "Produces utilisation and revenue reports." "Java"
            search = container "Search Service" "Finds vehicles by location and class." "Go"
            scheduler = container "Batch Scheduler" "Runs the nightly pricing and maintenance batch." "Java"
            fleetdb = container "Fleet Database" "Stores vehicle and booking records." "PostgreSQL"
            customerdb = container "Customer Database" "Stores customer and contract records." "PostgreSQL"
            mediadb = container "Media Database" "Stores contracts, invoices, and damage photos." "PostgreSQL"
            queue = container "Event Queue" "Carries fleet events between the application parts." "Kafka"
            rates = container "Pricing Rules Library" "Computes rental prices from class, duration, and zone." "Python"
        }
        payments = element "Payment Provider" "Charges customer cards for rentals and deposits."
        telemetryFeed = element "Vehicle Telemetry Feed" "Streams position and status telemetry." "MQTT" "External"
        legacy = softwareSystem "Legacy Billing System" "The retired billing system being phased out."
        customer -> booking "Rents vehicles through" "HTTPS"
        customer -> mobile "Books vehicles via" "HTTPS"
        booking -> fleet "Reserves vehicles in" "gRPC"
        booking -> pricing "uses" "HTTP"
        mobile -> dispatch "Requests dispatch via" "gRPC"
        fleet -> scheduler "Registers nightly tasks in" "gRPC"
        pricing -> rates "Looks up rules in" "in-process"
        contracts -> payments "Charges cards through" "REST/JSON"
        damage -> mediadb "Stores damage photos in" "SQL"
        reports -> fleetdb "Reads booking records from" "SQL"
        maintenance -> fleetdb "Stores service records in" "SQL"
        search -> fleetdb "Reads availability from" "SQL"
        contracts -> customerdb "Stores contract records in" "SQL"
        telemetry -> queue "Publishes telemetry events to" "Kafka"
        queue -> notifications "Delivers booking events to" "Kafka"
        telemetry -> telemetryFeed "Receives fleet telemetry from" "MQTT"
    }
    views {
        systemContext manager "CustomerContext" "Shows the customer's journey around the system." {
            include *
            autoLayout
        }
        container manager {
            include *
            autoLayout
        }
    }
}`;

const [validate, inspect, ctxExport, containerExport] = await Promise.allSettled([
  tools.structurizr.validate({ dsl }),
  tools.structurizr.inspect({ dsl }),
  tools.structurizr["export-plantuml"]({ dsl, viewKey: "CustomerContext" }),
  tools.structurizr["export-plantuml"]({ dsl, viewKey: "Containers" }),
]);

const show = (r) => r.status === "fulfilled" ? r.value : { error: String(r.reason) };
return {
  validate: show(validate),
  inspect: show(inspect),
  ctxExport: show(ctxExport),
  containerExport: show(containerExport),
};

part.text:
I read the model, ran it through Structurizr (`validate` + `inspect`), and exported both views to see exactly what renders. The model on disk is untouched — all checks were in-memory.

**Validation:** parses cleanly (`OK`). **Inspection:** 6 errors (no workspace scope; Fleet Manager has containers but no linked documentation/decisions; Legacy Billing System is disconnected and on no view; container view has an auto-generated key).

## Findings

**Errors (wrong abstraction / notation / broken view)**

- **`rates` "Pricing Rules Library" (container)** — A library is not a runtime boundary; C4 containers must be separately-running processes or data stores. The `pricing -> rates "Looks up rules in" "in-process"` relationship confirms it lives inside the Pricing Service. It should be a *component* of `pricing` (or dropped). Matters because it misrepresents the runtime/deployment topology — readers will assume a separate Python service to run, scale, and monitor.
- **`legacy` "Legacy Billing System" (softwareSystem)** — Disconnected: no relationships to/from it, and it appears on *neither* rendered view (confirmed by inspection: "not included on any views"). Matters because it's dead weight; if it's truly "retired / being phased out" it likely shouldn't be in the current model at all, or a migration relationship should show why it's still referenced.
- **`payments` "Payment Provider" (element)** — Modeled as a generic `element` rather than a `softwareSystem`, and not tagged `External` (unlike `telemetryFeed`). Matters because external systems should be software systems and consistently distinguished as external.
- **`telemetryFeed` "Vehicle Telemetry Feed" (element)** — Also a generic `element` rather than a `softwareSystem` (it is tagged `External`, which is good, but the type is wrong). Same notation inconsistency.
- **System context view `CustomerContext`** — The rendered view only shows the customer's *web* journey (`Customer → Fleet Manager: "Rents vehicles through"`). The mobile journey (`customer -> mobile "Books vehicles via"`) is dropped when container-level relationships are promoted to system level. Matters because the view is titled "CustomerContext" and described as "Shows the customer's journey around the system," yet it omits half the journey. The model relies on lossy implicit promotion; the context view needs explicit person→system relationships.

**Warnings (vague labels, description/relationship mismatches, completeness)**

- **`booking -> pricing "uses" "HTTP"` (relationship)** — Vague label. Matters because it doesn't say what is used for; e.g. "requests price quotes from."
- **`queue` "Event Queue" + `telemetry -> queue` + `queue -> notifications` (relationships)** — Inconsistent event flow. The queue is described as carrying "fleet events," but the only producer (`telemetry`) publishes *telemetry* events and the only consumer (`notifications`) receives *booking* events. Nothing publishes booking events, and nothing consumes telemetry events. Matters because the queue's stated purpose contradicts the edges, and the trigger for notifications is missing.
- **`scheduler` "Batch Scheduler" + `fleet -> scheduler` (relationship)** — The scheduler is described as "Runs the nightly pricing and maintenance batch," but its only edge is `fleet -> scheduler "Registers nightly tasks in"`. There are no edges from `scheduler` to `pricing` or `maintenance`. Matters because the diagram never shows what the batch actually does.
- **`contracts`, `damage`, `reports`, `search`, `maintenance` (containers)** — No incoming relationships; nothing in the model reaches them. Matters because they render as isolated boxes with only outgoing edges (to DBs/external); e.g. the booking flow presumably creates contracts and searches for vehicles, but `booking` has no edge to `contracts` or `search`.
- **`fleetdb` "Fleet Database" (container)** — Described as "Stores vehicle and booking records," but no container writes booking records to it (`booking` has no edge to `fleetdb`). Matters because the writer for the primary records is missing, leaving the data flow incomplete.
- **`mediadb` "Media Database" (container)** — Described as "Stores contracts, invoices, and damage photos," but only damage photos are written (`damage -> mediadb`); contracts actually go to `customerdb`, and nothing writes invoices. Matters because the description overstates and contradicts the relationships.
- **`customerdb` "Customer Database" (container)** — Described as "Stores customer and contract records," but only contract records are written. Minor description/relationship mismatch.
- **`mobile` "Mobile Backend" (container)** — The customer "Books vehicles via" it, but its only edge is `mobile -> dispatch`. It has no edges to `contracts`, `pricing`, `search`, or `fleetdb`, unlike the web path. Matters because the mobile booking path is asymmetric/incomplete — it's unclear how a mobile booking is recorded or priced.
- **`fleetdb`, `customerdb`, `mediadb` (containers)** — No `Database` tag/shape, so they render as plain rectangles rather than cylinders. Matters because it loses the visual convention that distinguishes data stores from services.

**Suggestions (style / organization / optional)**

- **Workspace** — No scope defined (inspection error); set it to `SoftwareSystem` or `Landscape`.
- **`manager` "Fleet Manager" (softwareSystem)** — Has containers but no linked documentation or decisions (inspection errors); C4 best practice is to attach ADRs/docs once a system has containers.
- **Container view** — Auto-generated key `Container-001` (unstable over time); give the view an explicit name/key.
- **`queue` "Event Queue" (container)** — No `Queue` tag/shape; message brokers are usually visually distinguished.
- **People** — Only `customer` is modeled. The operational services (`maintenance`, `reports`, `scheduler`, `damage`) imply internal staff (fleet managers, mechanics, analysts) who aren't represented. If the model is meant to cover more than the customer journey, those personas are a completeness gap.
- **Styling** — No `!theme`/style block; external elements aren't visually distinguished (only one carries the `External` tag).

## Completeness & positives

The model is **internally sparse**: 18 containers, but the relationship graph leaves several services unreachable and the queue/scheduler flows inconsistent with their descriptions. The two required views (system context + container) both exist and render, every element has a name and description, all inter-container relationships carry a protocol, and there are no bidirectional edges — those are the strengths. The highest-value fixes are: demote `rates` to a component, remove or connect `legacy`, type `payments`/`telemetryFeed` as `softwareSystem`, add explicit person→system relationships so the context view shows the full customer journey, and reconcile the queue/scheduler/DB descriptions with the edges that actually exist.
